reasoning.text: The render is genuinely strong: TOP cleanly resolves eight blue BRAM banks, the copper multiplier column, the symmetric add/sub comb, the Barrett reduction spine and the offset exploded cluster, while FRONT/SIDE confirm everything rests on the ground line with the read/twiddle/return buses on standoffs and the heatsink correctly lifted on its riser. The visual axes are at their ceiling. The two soft spots versus the rubric were (a) recognizability — a bare placed-and-routed board reads as a generic PCB because the most iconic accelerator-card cue, a host edge connector, was absent and the data path had no origin; and (b) proportional grounding cited too few dimensional facts. The deepest unresolved failure is still buildability: the headline conflict-free bank/offset equations, the modulus q, psi/omega and the FSM table remain reproduction defaults, honestly flagged but not the paper's verified values, so a competent engineer cannot yet rebuild it bit-exactly.
gaps: Transcribe the paper's actual Sec. III conflict-free bank-index/offset functions (its headline result) into crossbar_network and addr_gen_unit and reconcile with o(i)=i>>3 — this is the single largest remaining buildability gain (~2-3 pts) and is the reason this pass is not converged.
Replace q=12289 (reproduction default) with the paper's benchmark modulus and recompute mu (currently 21843 at k=28) and N_inv (currently 8857 = 1024^-1 mod 12289).
Pin a concrete primitive 2048-th root psi mod q and store its power table in twiddle_rom.spec for bit-exactness; psi/omega are currently given only by their defining congruences.
Verify schedule_controller.fsm transition table and the stage/block loop bounds against the paper's scheduling figure and confirm they yield the 33% mult / 20% add-sub counts.
Confirm pipeline latencies (mult 3 / add-sub 1 / Barrett 4 / reg 1 = 9) against the paper's reported cycle counts and clock for the 1024-pt 8-BU radix-4 core.
Visual axes are at ceiling — do not add further decorative parts; future gains must come from source-grounded numbers, not geometry.

fields.before: Streams raw input coefficients into the head BRAM banks in natural order at the start of the forward NTT pass.
fields.after: Streams raw input coefficients from the host controller into the head BRAM banks in natural order at the start of the forward NTT pass.

fields.before: Drains transformed coefficients out of the tail banks in natural order, eliminating the bit-reversal pass.
fields.after: Drains transformed coefficients out of the tail banks in natural order back to the host controller, eliminating the bit-reversal pass.

fields.before: EXPLODED ABOVE: aluminum heatsink baseplate that clamps onto the FPGA package lid covering the whole die, lifted off here on a riser stub so the die floorplan stays visible.
fields.after: EXPLODED ABOVE: aluminum heatsink baseplate that clamps onto the FPGA package lid covering the whole die, lifted off here on a riser stub so the die floorplan stays visible; carries ten fins at 0.3 pitch.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame); cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the seven-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
meta.after: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame); cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the ten-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
